title: About - Studio Torsten Posselt
description: STP is a multidisciplinary design studio that focuses on the creation and production of bespoke artworks and design applications.
heading: About
introduction: STP is a design studio where art direction runs through everything — branding, editorial, packaging, spatial installation, whether for a record label or a global brand. We work at every scale, for clients who want the work to carry weight.
clients: Clients and partners include Nils Frahm, Ólafur Arnalds, Kiasmos, Barbican Centre, Leiter, Erased Tapes Records, Universal Music, Reebok, Volkswagen Group, Wikimedia, Manners McDade, Leiter, and Reeperbahn Festival.
bio: Torsten Posselt (b. 1979, Dresden) is a graphic designer, visual artist, and art director. He studied visual communication and printmaking at the University of Arts, Berlin (UdK).

In 2011 he co-founded FELD, a Berlin-based design studio, where he served as managing partner and design director until 2019 — leading brand identity and design projects for Reebok, Volkswagen, the Fraunhofer Institute, and the Barbican Centre. He founded Studio Torsten Posselt in 2020 to work under his own name and on his own terms.

Posselt works across branding, editorial, and packaging – with art direction as the discipline that holds it together. His visual identities give organisations a coherent language to work from; his artwork for Nils Frahm and Ólafur Arnalds, released through labels including Erased Tapes, Mercury KX, and Leiter, has become part of how listeners understand those artists, inseparable from the music.

He lectures and runs workshops on design process and packaging. His work appears in [MIN – The New Simplicity in Graphic Design](https://thamesandhudson.com/min-9780500292198) and [Collector's Edition – Innovative Packaging and Graphics](https://thamesandhudson.com/collector-s-edition-9780500517574) by Stuart Tolley as well as [Album Art – New Music Graphics](https://thamesandhudson.com/album-art-9780500294154) by John Foster, published by Thames and Hudson.
